title: The Witness
subtitle: The observer becomes vulnerable to the event recorded
sourceCredit: D. Parvaz · The Moth Radio Hour, “Bearing Witness”

shot.title: Looking through a notebook
shot.direction: The notebook initially frames a distant street. The scene is a preliminary dramatic concept, not verified incident footage.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Wide interior edge looking toward a distant ordinary street through an open door. The woman reporter stands in profile, notebook supported in one hand and pencil contacting its page with the other. The notebook and doorway quietly echo a viewfinder; no specific violence is visible in the street.

shot.title: The view remains open
shot.direction: The reporter continues attending to the still-open street view. A slight body shift may begin, but the door remains open until the later command to close it.
shot.soundDirection: Open street ambience; door closure follows the later command.

illustration.direction: Wide interior edge looking toward a distant ordinary street through an open door. The woman reporter stands in profile, notebook supported in one hand and pencil contacting its page with the other. The notebook and doorway quietly echo a viewfinder; no specific violence is visible in the street.

beats.caption: I’m here to record what happens.
beats.speaker: REPORTER

shot.title: Here to record
shot.direction: The reporter writes while the street remains at a distance.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Wide interior edge looking toward a distant ordinary street through an open door. The woman reporter stands in profile, notebook supported in one hand and pencil contacting its page with the other. The notebook and doorway quietly echo a viewfinder; no specific violence is visible in the street.

shot.title: Close that door
shot.direction: A quiet command is followed by a broad door edge. Do not invent an identifiable captor.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Same viewpoint. The broad edge of the door enters the open street view, beginning to narrow it. The reporter pauses her pencil and lifts her gaze. No hand on the door, captor, struggle or cause of closure is shown. Her body remains naturally balanced.

shot.title: The available view narrows
shot.direction: The visible street narrows to a slit in a continuous, readable action.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: The door leaves a narrow vertical view of the street. The reporter reaches one open hand toward the remaining opening while holding the notebook against her torso with the other. The reaching gesture is cautious and ordinary, with no forced confrontation or physical restraint.

beats.caption: Wait. I need to see what’s happening.
beats.speaker: REPORTER

shot.title: Need to see
shot.direction: She reaches toward the view without an invented struggle or added incident detail.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: The door leaves a narrow vertical view of the street. The reporter reaches one open hand toward the remaining opening while holding the notebook against her torso with the other. The reaching gesture is cautious and ordinary, with no forced confrontation or physical restraint.

shot.title: Inside the frame
shot.direction: Her body and hands are now enclosed within the visual border she had treated as a viewfinder.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Wide small interior. The reporter is now visibly within the room and the doorway is almost shut. She lowers her reaching hand and looks at the notebook held close to her, shoulders tightened. The room boundary now surrounds her; there are no invented bars, chains or detention props.

beats.caption: This is no longer happening somewhere beyond me.
beats.speaker: REPORTER

shot.title: Not somewhere beyond me
shot.direction: Hold the recognition in her face and grip on the notebook.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Wide small interior. The reporter is now visibly within the room and the doorway is almost shut. She lowers her reaching hand and looks at the notebook held close to her, shoulders tightened. The room boundary now surrounds her; there are no invented bars, chains or detention props.

shot.title: The incomplete sentence
shot.direction: The pencil approaches the unfinished line but does not complete an invented conclusion.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Same room, seated woman and grounded chair fully coherent. The notebook lies open across her lap, one hand supporting its edge, pencil hovering above an unfinished faint mark. Her face registers recognition without theatrical terror. No readable writing and no completed conclusion.

shot.title: Room for testimony
shot.direction: An unfinished line reaches toward the page edge. Preserve the unresolved account.
shot.soundDirection: Street ambience muted by a closing door; pencil tip hanging over paper.

illustration.direction: Wide quiet interior held on the reporter, open notebook and a little doorway light. Her pencil remains suspended, eyes turned toward the edge of the page. Leave generous empty space beside her and preserve uncertainty; no escape, release, rescue or final fate is added.
